stem: A pyramid has a square base with sides of ${=b}$ cm. Its four triangular faces are identical, and each has a slant height of ${=s}$ cm (the height of the triangle, measured up the face from the middle of a base edge to the apex). Calculate the total surface area of the pyramid in $\text{cm}^{2}$.
solution: The surface of the pyramid is the square base together with four identical triangular faces, so $\text{surface area}=\text{area of base}+4\times\text{area of one triangular face}$.

Each triangular face has base ${=b}$ cm and height equal to the slant height ${=s}$ cm, so the four faces together have area $4\times\frac{1}{2}\times b\times h_s=4\times\frac{1}{2}\times{=b}\times{=s}={=2*b*s}\text{ cm}^{2}$.
notes: Entry point of the skill, modelled on ex13-7-10 and ex13-4-4: square base plus four triangles, with the slant height given and no vertical height to confuse it. Whole numbers throughout; b from 4 to 14, slant height always above half the base so the pyramid exists. Stem defines slant height in words because no figure is available.
